title: Why Traditional Education Can Never Work
author: Patrick Dempsey
summary: Patrick Dempsey continues a series arguing against the view that students must master facts before using AI, by offering a formula for how learning works. His model says a learner's new world model equals the old one multiplied by one plus genuine challenge, embodied agency, threshold concepts and deliberate practice. Because the terms are multiplied, learning stalls if any term is zero, which he demonstrates with training wheels, which remove the challenge of balance, and with the marshmallow tower task in which kindergarteners outperform MBA students through rapid building and testing. He contrasts this with an additive view of traditional education, in which more lectures, facts and assignments are assumed to produce more knowledge. He argues this explains why AI feels threatening to a facts-based system while leaving teachers essential roles in designing challenges, adapting them in real time and timing threshold concepts. The piece is a theory-of-learning argument that previews a follow-up breaking down each component.
points: The proposed formula treats learning as multiplicative, so a missing component such as challenge or agency zeroes out learning regardless of how much of the rest is present.
Training wheels fail the formula because they do the balancing, removing the genuine challenge and feedback that bike riding requires.
Kindergarteners beat MBA students at the marshmallow tower because they build and test constantly, revising their model of the problem on each attempt.
Traditional education is framed as additive (more lectures, facts and assignments), which he says does not change understanding.
If learning is network transformation rather than fact accumulation, teachers remain essential for designing challenges, adapting them and delivering threshold concepts at the right moment.
quotes: Multiplication means that if any single component equals zero, the entire right side of the equation equals zero. Zero times anything is still zero. Which means, learning takes some greater-than-zero value for each of genuine challenge (GC), embodied agency (EA), threshold concepts (TC), and deliberate practice (DP).

Your understanding of what it takes to ride a bike (WM) remains uninformed and unformed. That is, whatever you don’t know about balance before you learn to ride with training wheels is exactly what you still don’t know about balance after!

This is where the 5-year-olds really excel. Because they are building and testing as a default, they are constantly developing threshold concepts: “marshmallow is heavy,” “triangle is stable,” “bottom needs to be wide.” TCs keep showing up every time they try.

At that point, they totally get it. And at this point, their world models break in the best way. Even if they haven’t figured out a better solution to the final design of the tower, their model now recognizes that they need to build and test, and that is indeed transformative, albeit if too late.

Because they are building so quickly and testing so frequently, they are creating new models with every single attempt at the tower! By the end of the 18 minutes, they are likely on their tenth model or more of what it takes to accomplish the challenge!
AI can generate facts and outputs instantly. So if learning = facts and outputs to capture them, then AI 100% makes teachers obsolete.
